answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable membership bond before it can submit work, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled audit proves the work fraudulent. The bond does not prove a person’s identity; it makes identities costly to multiply and gives auditors a concrete penalty to enforce. An attacker seeking influence across a grove of agents must lock a bond for every identity, tying up capital and risking losses, whether each agent sends a sonnet or reports an opal.
